title: How CROs Can Lead on Climate Resilience
gist: Global weather- and climate-related direct economic losses hit roughly $277 billion in 2025 with less than half ($125 billion) insured, and the World Economic Forum estimates physical risks could jeopardize 5%-25% of EBITDA by 2050 for non-adapting companies. BCG argues the chief risk officer, not the sustainability function, should own physical climate risk — quantifying it in NPV/IRR terms so resilience capex competes with other uses of capital, as a European highway operator did when it raised over EUR 5 billion of sustainable finance to cut expected climate losses by up to 40%.

themes.theme: Loss Escalation and the Widening Insurance Gap

insights.claim: Global direct economic losses from weather- and climate-related events reached approximately $277 billion in 2025, of which less than half ($125 billion) was insured, per reinsurance broker Gallagher Re.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A ~$150 billion uninsured annual loss pool sits directly on corporate and sovereign balance sheets, not insurers' — screen holdings by uninsured physical exposure, not by insured-loss headlines.
insights.quote: In 2025, global direct economic losses from weather- and climate-related events reached approximately $277 billion, according to Gallagher Re, a reinsurance broker.
insights.locator: Physical Risk Is Already Material—and Intensifying

insights.claim: Average annual losses from climate events have roughly doubled in real terms since the early 1990s, driven by greater frequency and severity of events rather than by nominal inflation.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A real-terms doubling over ~35 years is a structural trend line, not noise — underwriting and asset models calibrated on pre-2000 history are systematically light.
insights.quote: average annual losses have roughly doubled in real terms since the early 1990s, owing to the greater frequency and severity of climate events

insights.claim: The gap between economic and insured climate losses is expected to widen further as insurers reprice or withdraw from high-risk markets, shifting loss absorption from insurers onto corporates.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Watch for insurer withdrawal in specific geographies as a leading indicator of forced self-insurance and impaired collateral values in property- and infrastructure-heavy sectors.
insights.quote: the insurance gap is set to widen as insurers reprice or withdraw from high-risk markets
insights.locator: At the same time, the insurance gap

insights.claim: A 2024 World Economic Forum analysis estimates that by 2050 physical climate risks could jeopardize 5% to 25% of EBITDA for companies that do not adapt, with the range depending on sector.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A 5%-25% EBITDA haircut is a valuation-level input, not an ESG footnote — the sector dispersion inside that range is where relative-value trades sit.
insights.quote: by 2050, physical risks could jeopardize 5% to 25% of EBITDA for companies that don't adapt, depending on the sector
insights.locator: A 2024 World Economic Forum analysis estimates

insights.claim: Headline direct-loss figures understate true economic cost because they exclude indirect impacts such as productivity losses and business interruption.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Assume reported catastrophe loss tallies are a floor; second-order interruption costs land in operating margins one to two quarters after the event.
insights.quote: The true economic cost, including indirect impacts such as productivity losses and business interruption, is likely to be significantly higher.
insights.locator: The true economic cost, including indirect impacts

themes.theme: Value-Chain Blind Spots Beyond Owned Assets

insights.claim: The least-managed category of physical climate risk is exposure to assets and infrastructure a company relies on but does not own or operate.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Company disclosures that cover only owned property systematically miss the largest exposure — treat 'we assessed our facilities' as an incomplete answer in diligence.
insights.quote: many are not set up to manage these risks strategically, particularly those related to assets and infrastructure that they rely on but don’t own or operate.
insights.locator: Although some organizations are starting to act

insights.claim: Most companies' visibility into supplier climate exposure stops at tier 1, leaving no consistent view of material exposure across the full value chain.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Concentration risk in tier 2/3 nodes is effectively unpriced; single-source upstream chokepoints in flood- or heat-exposed regions are the hidden tail.
insights.quote: Fragmentation across functions—and limited visibility beyond tier 1 suppliers—prevents a consistent view of material exposure along the full value chain.
insights.locator: The CRO Challenge: Rising Expectations, Constrained Capabilities

insights.claim: Even when climate risks are identified, they are typically assessed qualitatively and in functional silos, and are never translated into financial terms usable for capital allocation or strategic planning.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Qualitative heat-map disclosure is a signal the company cannot yet defend its resilience capex — a management-quality differentiator worth probing on calls.
insights.quote: Even where risks are identified, they’re often assessed qualitatively and in silos within functions.
insights.locator: Although many companies perform advanced risk identification

insights.claim: Physical climate damage transmits to the P&L through four distinct channels: revenue lost to operational disruption, asset damage and impairment, higher capex and opex to repair and adapt assets, and volatile input costs plus delays across the value chain.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete line-item map for stress-testing a company model rather than applying a blanket 'climate discount'.
insights.locator: These risks are translating into material financial impacts

insights.claim: Physical climate risk assessment must be built on forward-looking climate scenarios rather than historical loss data, because past experience structurally understates future exposure.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Any actuarial or credit model still anchored on backward-looking catastrophe history is mispriced by construction — a source of adverse selection for insurers and lenders.
insights.quote: Physical risk assessment must draw on forward-looking climate scenarios rather than historical data, since past experience understates future exposure.
insights.locator: 1. Identify physical risks.

themes.theme: Relocating Climate Risk from Sustainability to the CRO

insights.claim: BCG argues the chief risk officer, not the sustainability function, is best placed to own physical climate risk because the CRO's mandate spans the enterprise and can embed it into the existing enterprise risk management framework.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Signals climate risk migrating out of the ESG reporting stack into core risk and finance — reporting-only ESG tooling loses relevance, risk-quantification vendors gain.
insights.quote: The chief risk officer is best placed to move toward a more quantified and strategic approach to managing physical risks.
insights.locator: The chief risk officer is best placed

insights.claim: Physical climate risk should be quantified in the same financial language already used for cyber and legal risk, so that leaders can compare it objectively against other exposures.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Comparability is the unlock: once climate loss is expressed like cyber loss, resilience spend competes for capital instead of being an out-of-budget mandate.
insights.locator: 2. Quantify risks in financial terms.

insights.claim: The CRO role is shifting from reporting on risk to enabling the investments and decisions required to manage it, while the CEO and board retain overall accountability.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: An expanding CRO remit means budget migration toward risk analytics, scenario modeling, and integrated monitoring platforms.
insights.quote: The CRO role is evolving, from reporting on risk to enabling the decisions and investments required to manage it.
insights.locator: Yet this moment also represents a significant opportunity.

insights.claim: Companies face three comparable financial responses to physical climate exposure — retain the risk, reduce it via resilience investment, or transfer it via insurance — evaluated on NPV, IRR, or avoided losses.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: As insurance repricing makes transfer expensive, the retain-vs-reduce trade shifts toward capex — a durable demand driver for adaptation and hardening contractors.
insights.quote: retaining the risk, reducing the company’s exposure through resilience investment, or transferring the risk through insurance
insights.locator: 3. Embed physical risk into strategic decisions

insights.claim: Risk appetite thresholds themselves need board-approved adjustment, particularly for chronic climate stressors that accumulate into material exposure over time rather than arriving as discrete acute events.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Chronic stressors (heat, subsidence, water stress) escape event-triggered risk registers entirely — a slow-burn impairment channel with no catastrophe headline to flag it.
insights.quote: Risk appetite thresholds also need to be adjusted (with board approval), particularly for chronic risks that can accumulate into material exposure over time.
insights.locator: Risk appetite thresholds also need to be adjusted

insights.claim: Climate risk disclosure should be directed at boards and investors as financially grounded risk insight rather than as sustainability reporting.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Expect the disclosure center of gravity to move from sustainability reports into risk and MD&A sections — a tell for which issuers have actually quantified exposure.
insights.quote: CROs can ensure that the board and investors see financially grounded risk insights, rather than sustainability disclosures.
insights.locator: 5. Report physical risks and resilience

insights.claim: Resilience should be integrated into day-to-day operations and business decisions rather than run as a standalone initiative, and monitored via KPIs tied to measurable risk reduction such as lower expected annual losses.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: 'Expected annual loss reduction' is the metric to demand from management — it is auditable, unlike qualitative resilience narratives.
insights.quote: The overarching goal is to integrate resilience measures into day-to-day operations—and into business decisions—as opposed to addressing them through a standalone initiative.
insights.locator: 4. Execute and monitor the resilience strategy.

themes.theme: European Motorway Case: Financing Adaptation at Scale

insights.claim: A major European highway operator assessed physical climate risk across more than 3,000 kilometers of motorway including roughly 4,000 bridges, viaducts, and tunnels, finding flooding and extreme precipitation the biggest hazards and bridges the key vulnerability points.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Concession-based infrastructure with long asset lives and tolling revenue is the clearest place where climate capex directly reprices cash flows.
insights.quote: more than 3,000 kilometers of motorway, including approximately 4,000 bridges, viaducts, and tunnels
insights.locator: Managing Climate Risks to Roadways in Europe

insights.claim: The European highway operator raised over EUR 5 billion through sustainable finance instruments, including more than EUR 1 billion from the European Investment Bank, to fund bridge and tunnel reinforcement, slope stabilization, and drainage improvements.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Demonstrates a live funding channel: quantified physical risk unlocks multi-billion sustainable-debt issuance, with development banks anchoring the book.
insights.quote: the company raised over €5 billion through sustainable finance instruments, including more than €1 billion from the European Investment Bank
insights.locator: To finance this strategy

insights.claim: The highway operator's adaptation investments are expected to reduce the financial impact from climate-related events by up to 40%.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A quantified 40% loss-reduction claim is the kind of number that supports resilience ROI underwriting — and the kind investors should ask to see verified ex post.
insights.quote: These investments are expected to reduce the financial impact from climate-related events by up to 40%.
insights.locator: These investments are expected to reduce

insights.claim: Disruption to a national motorway network threatened cascading effects across almost all value chains in the country, extending the loss beyond the asset owner itself.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Single points of national infrastructure failure propagate into unrelated sectors — a systemic correlation that portfolio-level climate models usually miss.
insights.quote: disruption to critical infrastructure threatened cascading effects across almost all value chains in the country
insights.locator: Moreover, disruption to critical infrastructure

themes.theme: Emerging Market Infrastructure for Pricing Resilience

insights.claim: Open Sesame, launched in May 2026 as a joint initiative of the World Business Council for Sustainable Development and the Federation of European Risk Management Associations with BCG support, aims to help companies price in physical risk, reward resilience performance, and finance resilience more efficiently.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
entities: World Business Council for Sustainable Development
Federation of European Risk Management Associations
insights.so_what: Cross-industry standardization is the precondition for resilience to earn a cost-of-capital or premium discount — watch whether insurers and banks actually adopt it.
insights.quote: Open Sesame, launched in May 2026, is a joint initiative of the World Business Council for Sustainable Development and the Federation of European Risk Management Associations, with support from BCG.
insights.locator: New Resources to Quantify the Impact of Resilience Efforts

insights.claim: The Institutional Investors Group on Climate Change launched the Climate Resilience Investment Framework in June 2025 to help investors assess and manage physical climate risk across portfolios, with an initial focus on real estate and infrastructure.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
entities: Institutional Investors Group on Climate Change
insights.so_what: Real estate and infrastructure get screened first — expect resilience-linked dispersion in cap rates and asset-level valuations in those two sectors before others.
insights.quote: the Institutional Investors Group on Climate Change launched the Climate Resilience Investment Framework in June 2025
insights.locator: From the investor side

insights.claim: As investors increasingly use the Climate Resilience Investment Framework to assess corporate physical risk management, companies gain an incentive to align their internal risk quantification and reporting with that framework's expectations.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Investor-side frameworks, not regulation, may become the binding constraint on corporate climate risk disclosure quality.
insights.locator: As investors increasingly use CRIF

insights.claim: External pressure on companies from tightening insurance markets, regulators, and investors is accelerating faster than companies' internal capability to quantify and manage physical climate risk.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A widening capability-versus-expectation gap creates a consulting, data, and analytics spend cycle — and a compliance-shock risk for laggard issuers.
insights.quote: External expectations are accelerating faster than internal capabilities, with tightening insurance markets and increasing regulatory and investor pressure.
insights.locator: The CRO Challenge: Rising Expectations, Constrained Capabilities

insights.claim: Integrated physical risk management across operations and the full value chain is framed as a potential source of competitive differentiation rather than a compliance cost.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: If resilience is a differentiator, it shows up as lower earnings volatility and cheaper insurance — testable in the numbers, not just in the narrative.
insights.quote: Integrated physical risk management across operations and the value chain can become a core differentiator in how companies compete.
insights.locator: As extreme weather events grow in frequency
